rules.title: [PL] Mitchi rules
rules.intro: [PL] Everything you need to play, from setup to the end of the game.

overview.heading: [PL] Overview
overview.summary: [PL] Mitchi is a dice game for two or more players, played over a series of rounds. Each round, you roll to avoid being left with the worst hand. The player with the worst hand takes the points in the pot. When the game ends, the player with the fewest points wins.

youNeed.heading: [PL] What you need
youNeed.paper: [PL] A pen and paper to keep score

setup.heading: [PL] Setup
setup.pointLimit: [PL] Agree a point limit. 25 is usual. Choose a lower limit for a shorter game.
setup.whoStarts: [PL] Decide who starts. Everyone rolls one die, and the highest roll starts. If the highest roll is tied, those players roll again. Play goes clockwise.

hands.heading: [PL] Hands
hands.intro: [PL] A hand is the two dice you finish your turn with. There are six groups of hands, from best to worst:
hands.allHandsLink: [PL] All hands are listed on the <reference>quick reference</reference>.

rollLimit.heading: [PL] The starting player sets the roll limit
rollLimit.rolls: [PL] The starting player rolls both dice, up to three times, and can stop after any roll. After each roll, they can:
rollLimit.keepOne: [PL] keep one die and re-roll the other
rollLimit.newChoice: [PL] Each roll is a new choice. Keeping a die on one roll does not mean keeping it on the next. Re-rolling one die still counts as a roll.
rollLimit.setsLimit: [PL] The number of rolls the starting player uses is the <term>roll limit</term> for everyone else that round.
rollLimit.example: [PL] The starting player rolls six-three in two rolls. Everyone else gets up to two rolls.

everyoneElse.heading: [PL] Everyone else
everyoneElse.turn: [PL] Everyone else takes a turn in clockwise order, with the same choices, up to the roll limit. You do not have to use every roll. Stop when you are happy with your hand.
everyoneElse.worstHandSoFar: [PL] You never need the best hand. You only need to beat the <term>worst hand so far</term>: the lowest-ranked hand rolled this round. It changes as players finish their turn, so a later player may have less to beat than an earlier one.
everyoneElse.example1: [PL] Player 1 rolls six-four in one. Player 2 rolls five-one. Player 3 now needs five-two or better, because five-one is the worst hand so far.
everyoneElse.example2: [PL] Player 1 rolls five-four in three. Player 2 rolls six-two in one. That already beats five-four, so Player 2 stops.

scoring.heading: [PL] Scoring the round
scoring.startingPot: [PL] Every round starts with 1 point in <term>the pot</term>.
scoring.mitchis: [PL] The first Mitchi rolled replaces that point with 2 points. Each Mitchi after that adds 2 more, so the pot is 2 points for every Mitchi rolled.
scoring.takeThePot: [PL] At the end of the round, the player with the worst hand <term>takes the pot</term> and adds the points to their score. They start the next round.

tieBreaks.heading: [PL] Tie-breaks
tieBreaks.intro: [PL] If two or more players are tied on the worst hand, they play a <term>tie-break</term> to decide who takes the pot.
tieBreaks.rollOnce: [PL] Roll once each. Only the tied players roll, with no re-rolls. Go in the opposite direction to the last round or tie-break, starting with the last player to roll.
tieBreaks.addMitchis: [PL] Add 2 points for each Mitchi rolled in the tie-break.
tieBreaks.worstHandTakes: [PL] The worst hand takes the pot. If players tie again, go back to step 1 with only those players.

example.tied: [PL] Three players tie on the worst hand
example.takesPot: [PL] One player has the worst hand and takes the pot

winning.heading: [PL] Winning the game
winning.gameEnds: [PL] The game ends when any player reaches the point limit. The player with the fewest points wins.
winning.tiedOnFewest: [PL] If players are tied on the fewest points, they roll once each, and the best hand wins.

reference.title: [PL] Quick reference
reference.intro: [PL] Everything you need mid-game, on one screen.

ranking.heading: [PL] Hand ranking
ranking.intro: [PL] Best at the top, worst at the bottom. Within a group, the higher hand wins. The worst hand in the game is three-one.
ranking.tableCaption: [PL] Mitchi hands, ranked from best to worst

scoring.heading: [PL] Scoring
scoring.intro: [PL] Every round starts with 1 point in the pot. The first Mitchi replaces it with 2 points, and each Mitchi after that adds 2 more. The worst hand takes the pot and starts the next round.

tieBreaks.heading: [PL] Tie-breaks
tieBreaks.intro: [PL] Tied players roll once each. The worst hand takes the pot.
tieBreaks.eachMitchi: [PL] Each Mitchi rolled in a tie-break

pointLimit.heading: [PL] Point limit
pointLimit.summary: [PL] The game ends when any player reaches the point limit, usually 25. The fewest points wins. If players are tied on the fewest points, they roll once each and the best hand wins.

about.title: [PL] About Mitchi
about.intro: [PL] What the game is, and where it came from.

game.heading: [PL] The game
game.summary: [PL] Mitchi is a fast dice game for two or more players. Each round, you roll to avoid the worst hand. Whoever ends up with it takes points. The player with the fewest points wins. You need two dice, a pen and paper, and at least one other player.

origin.heading: [PL] Where it came from
origin.learnt: [PL] I learnt Mitchi while I was living in Sanlúcar de Barrameda, in southern Spain. A group of us used to meet at La Gitana after work and play on the bar top.
origin.cousin: [PL] My cousin taught us, and it caught on quickly. I don't know where he learnt it, and I've never come across it anywhere else. I couldn't find the rules written down either, so I've put them here for anyone who wants to learn.

whyItStuck.heading: [PL] Why it stuck
whyItStuck.easy: [PL] It's easy to learn and quick to play. Rounds are fast, and you only need two dice and somewhere to roll them.
whyItStuck.tactical: [PL] It's tactical too. Everyone can see the scores, so every round matters, and once the Mitchis start rolling, the pot soon climbs.

relatedGames.heading: [PL] Related games
relatedGames.intro: [PL] Mitchi is not the only game where a 2 and a 1 is the best hand. While building this site I came across a couple of others, and there are probably more.
relatedGames.mia: [PL] Mia: the dice are rolled in secret under a cup, and players call out their hand. They can bluff.
relatedGames.mexico: [PL] Mexico: players roll to avoid the lowest hand, losing a life each time, until one player is left.
